messages:
kevin: Ran the slo-driven batcher job overnight against canary routes (tier=prod-high, prod-low). p95 jumped on prod-low for long-context chat routes. attaching quick profiler output below.

kevin: profiler snapshot: microbatch_wait_ms=18, kv_deser_ms=42, kernel_dispatch_ms=210, total_p95=320ms (baseline was ~190ms before the change)

olivia: ugh. which change correlated? the kernel-selector tweak or the token-budget cap?

kevin: initial suspect = token-budget reallocation. we increased per-request token_budget target to 160 for prod-low to improve throughput. but that raised microbatch sizes and triggered a fallback kernel path that is much slower for short-seq workloads.

sam: can you paste the token allocator config you used?

kevin: here:```yaml
batcher:
  slo_goal_p95_ms: 250
  route_overrides:
    prod-high:
      token_budget_target: 200
      max_microbatches: 8
    prod-low:
      token_budget_target: 160
      max_microbatches: 12
  queue_policy: oldest_first
```

maria: two quick things: 1) prod-low has worse KV hit-rate for those chat routes (we saw kv_hit_rate drop from 0.78 -> 0.61 after recent routing change). 2) kernel selector picks a fallback quantized kernel for batch_size>=6 for some models which is slower for small seq lengths due to extra packing/unpack overhead.

nic: re: KV – are we serializing the cache entries in the request path? I remember a change moved some cache operations onto the hot path last month.

kevin: yes, kv_deser_ms spike lines up with that commit. we now deserialize into a new vector type before merging, extra memcpy.

olivia: sounds like a triple hit: higher token targets -> larger microbatches -> kernel picks fallback slow path AND worse KV deserialization cost. That would explain p95 regressions.

sam: propose immediate mitigation: 1) enforce per-route microbatch cap of 6 for prod-low to avoid triggering fallback kernel 2) revert the KV deserialization change (or lazy-deserialize only when cache hit probability > threshold) 3) adjust token_budget_target to be SLO-aware, not throughput-first.

kevin: patched quick canary config and ran a small test: microbatch cap=6 + token_budget_target=120 -> kernel_dispatch_ms down to 120, kv_deser_ms down to 18, total_p95=180ms.

infra-bot: deploy:batcher-config canary applied to nodepool-canary-3 (cfg id 2026f). @kevin please monitor for 30m.

maria: long-term we probably need a cost function in kernel selector that considers seq_len distribution + microbatch_size and chooses the true latency-optimal path, not just FLOPS. Also prefetch KV into shared mmap buffer to avoid per-request allocations.

nic: agree on prefetch. we can also introduce a tiny per-route predictor that estimates kv_hit_rate and flips lazy-deser on/off. low hit rates skip deserialization.

olivia: rollout plan suggestion: A/B the token_budget controller (current vs SLO-driven) on 5% traffic for 24h, track p95, kv_deser_ms, kernel_dispatch_ms, microbatch_size_hist. If <5% regressions, escalate to 25%.

sam: +1. also add a realtime alert: if p95 > 1.3 * slo_goal for >5min then auto-revert canary token-budget changes and cap microbatches.

kevin: I'll prepare a profiling dashboard panel with three heatmaps: seq_len vs microbatch_size vs kernel_dispatch_ms, kv_hit_rate over time, and p95 per-route. Will post link when ready.

maria: FYI I found a minor perf regression in kernel runtime: the dispatch path for patched-op has a conditional that allocates an op-buffer per microbatch. simple fix queued in #4912.

kevin: thanks, please link PR. For now I've reverted the deserialization commit in the canary and enforced microbatch cap. Monitoring looks good after 20min: p95 back to ~185ms on canary routes.

olivia: nice work. next steps: 1) roll the SLO-driven allocator A/B 2) submit kernel selector improvement RFC 3) implement KV lazy-deser and mmap prefetch prototype.

nic: I'll take the mmap prefetch spike. can you assign me the canary metrics so I can correlate IO stalls?

kevin: assigning metrics: dashboard id = infra/batcher/p95-token-allocator-2026. tagging you.

sam: add notes to the perf playbook about this exact failure mode (token_budget -> kernel fallback -> kv penalty) so oncall can triage faster next time.

kevin: will add a short incident-like doc in #incidents if the canary stays stable. thanks all :thumbsup:
